ca-los-angeles-2026-cityattorney-roy-mar.name: Marissa Roy
ca-los-angeles-2026-cityattorney-roy-mar.bio: Deputy Attorney General at the California Department of Justice who began her career in the Los Angeles City Attorney's Office.

positions.stance: Would significantly expand the office's capacity to protect workers and pursue companies that steal wages, misclassify workers, or fail to provide safe conditions.
Would expand the office's capacity to protect renters from eviction and predatory landlords and enforce the City's renter protections.
Would file lawsuits against corporate polluters and direct recovered restitution money into greening communities.
Would hold corporations accountable and go after "junk fees, predatory lenders, and exploitative debt collectors."
Would initiate lawsuits to defend Angelenos from the Trump Administration's "attacks on our civil rights" and prosecute federal agents violating local laws.

ca-san-diego-2026-treasurer-nakawatase-s.name: Shirley Nakawatase
ca-san-diego-2026-treasurer-nakawatase-s.bio: Certified public accountant with more than 40 years of financial and tax experience who founded what is now HNK CPAs.

positions.stance: "Use disciplined oversight and transparent decisions to protect taxpayer dollars."
Would make county tax information clearer and services easier for residents and businesses to use.
Would bring a CPA's financial judgment to the County's investment and cash management responsibilities.
Wants the board to keep its focus on literacy, math and English proficiency, demand an implementation plan, and give educators curriculum, training and time.
Wants a school assignment system worth understanding, schools families trust, a cradle-to-college pathway, and stable teaching teams.
Supports disaggregating outcomes and putting staffing and resources where the gaps are, especially at schools serving the highest-need students.
Says SFUSD is in a fiscal crisis and families deserve direct answers on "What are we paying for, and who is it helping?"
Calls high-quality constituent service "the core job of a board member," pledging to be present and reachable in school communities.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-cheung-virginia.name: Virginia Cheung
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-cheung-virginia.bio: Nonprofit advancement director and single mother of a son in public school.

positions.stance: Would push for parent engagement, targeted supports for high-need students, and shelter and safety for immigrant and unhoused families to keep kids in class.
Would recruit and retain educators through competitive salaries and benefits and expand high-demand programs in every neighborhood.
Wants culturally responsive tools to identify student needs early and close disparities in math, literacy and college readiness.
"Our money must reach classrooms"; supports cutting waste, protecting essential programs and a data-driven budget.
Would demand transparency in budgeting, enrollment and program decisions and give working-class and immigrant families "a real seat at the table."

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-fisher-alida.name: Alida Fisher
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-fisher-alida.bio: Current San Francisco School Board member, special education advocate and former foster parent.

positions.stance: Supports "building equitable schools and programs that allow all students to thrive and grow."
Supports modernizing the district's financial, payroll and HR systems and creating 21st-century digital networks and policies.
"Committing to open communication and accountability in every decision."
Supports community-based solutions such as restorative practices and universal design for learning to build trust and ensure safety.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-hazelton-ryan.name: Ryan Hazelton
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-hazelton-ryan.bio: Executive Director of Mariposa Kids, a nonprofit out-of-school-time program provider at SFUSD elementary schools.

positions.stance: Supports a proximity-based assignment system with integration goals built in to increase predictability for families.
Wants every neighborhood school to be one families actively choose, with equitable resources across communities.
Wants quality before- and after-school programs treated "as essential infrastructure, not optional extras."
Supports co-locating health, mental health and family services at school sites.
Wants sanctuary schools "enforced in practice, not just in policy," with multilingual engagement beyond translation.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-kim-phil.name: Phil Kim
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-kim-phil.bio: San Francisco School Board President and former seventh-grade science teacher who worked for the San Francisco Unified School District.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-lee-laurance.name: Laurance Lee
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-lee-laurance.bio: SFUSD graduate who volunteers weekly helping kindergartners learn to read.

positions.stance: Wants clear goals for SFUSD, funded and tracked, with management held accountable for following through.
Would protect classroom staffing and scrutinize central-office growth, outside contracts and unnecessary change orders.
Supports "a simpler, fairer and more predictable assignment system while strengthening schools in every neighborhood."

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-tello-reina.name: Reina Tello
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-tello-reina.bio: SFUSD graduate, single mother and union member.

positions.stance: Will fight for a curriculum that every SFUSD student "can see themselves in."
Wants SFUSD to treat language access and family-facing policy as necessities.
Supports funding prevention: community schools, mental health supports and resources that reach students.
Supports vocational programs, bilingual education, ethnic studies and community partnerships over a one-size-fits-all approach.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-tung-tim.name: Tim Tung
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-boe-tung-tim.bio: SFUSD parent leader and public finance professional.

positions.stance: Would maintain a structurally balanced budget, build reserves, and plan ahead for the sunset of the Prop G educator parcel tax.
Wants the delayed move to a zone-based assignment system completed without further stalling, giving families predictability near home.
Would expand intervention time, high-impact literacy tutoring and programs like language immersion, with transparent cohort-level performance data.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-ball-elijah.name: Elijah Ball
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-ball-elijah.bio: Campus planner who has worked with colleges nationwide and four California community college districts.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-lace-monroe.name: Monroe Lace
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-lace-monroe.bio: Public school teacher and member of San Francisco's Human Rights Commission.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-lacroix-lea.name: Leah LaCroix
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-lacroix-lea.bio: Former San Francisco Youth Commissioner and local Democratic Party officer who serves on the board of Mama G's Street Dinners.

positions.stance: Supports greater public input and oversight to increase transparency at City College.
Supports growing course offerings "to reestablish trust with the students who need them."
Supports collaborating on a long-term plan for the board to secure stability, steering away from corporate management philosophies.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-lee-jeremy.name: Jeremy Lee
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-lee-jeremy.bio: Asset Manager at Chinatown Community Development Center and President of the Rose Pak Asian American Club.

positions.stance: Supports expanding high-demand sections, strengthening noncredit-to-credit pathways and growing certificate and career-education programs.
Supports more Cantonese sections, additional Cantonese faculty, and work toward a state-funded Cantonese language certificate.
Calls Free City College San Francisco's most effective public benefit program and says "we should be investing far more" in it.
Supports directing resources toward enrollment growth and high-demand programs "rather than treating program cuts as the only response."

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-mcfadden-bu.name: Bunny McFadden
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-mcfadden-bu.bio: Longtime high school and community college educator with a doctorate in education and a former PTA president.

positions.stance: Says "budget reflects values" and pledges to prioritize decisions that increase enrollment.
"I will protect Free City with everything I have in me."
Wants a positive, reciprocal relationship between City College and every city institution, from the school district to city departments.
Wants students treated as important voices and supports student organizing and leadership development.
Says every City College decision "should put education, educators, and those being educated ahead of other factors."

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-tam-erwin.name: Erwin Tam
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-4yr-tam-erwin.bio: Leads finance at CalHFA, the state's affordable housing lender, after advising more than 30 California community colleges on funding and facilities.

positions.stance: Says "CCSF is in a cycle of waste and mismanagement that threatens closure" and that he is running to fix it.

ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-partial-ferguso.name: Ruth Ferguson
ca-sanfrancisco-2026-ccb-partial-ferguso.bio: City College of San Francisco trustee, appointed in January, with a master's in public policy from UC Berkeley.

positions.stance: Supports protecting Free City and urging restoration of its full funding.
Would have City College market Free City through targeted, multilingual campaigns instead of mass mailings.
Believes "cost should never be the reason a San Franciscan doesn't enroll."
Voted to approve a balanced budget that protects City College's financial stability.
Pushed for a more transparent, easy-to-read budget and will keep making sure it stays that way.
"Every San Franciscan deserves access to what this office provides."
"Every property owner should pay their fair share."

tx-bexar-2026-da-wolff-jason.name: Jason Wolff
tx-bexar-2026-da-wolff-jason.bio: Former eight-year judge of Bexar County Court at Law No. 2, ten-year assistant district attorney and four-year defense attorney.

positions.stance: Says the DA's office "has been run into the ground" and pledges to bring talent and training back to the courthouse.
Would give discretion to assistant district attorneys.
Would support local law enforcement officers and "stand up to ego driven Judges."
Says "if you commit crimes in this town, you will regret it" and promises to be transparent.

tx-bexar-2026-bcad-p1-bayne-susan.name: Susan Bayne
tx-bexar-2026-bcad-p1-bayne-susan.bio: Retired psychotherapist with 30 years of experience and a citizen tax advocate.

positions.stance: Committed to "protecting homeowners from unfair spikes and advocating for taxpayer rights at every meeting."
Wants taxes calculated accurately and fairly through open appraisal processes and accessible data for all residents.

tx-bexar-2026-bcad-p1-arevalo-diana.name: Diana Arévalo
tx-bexar-2026-bcad-p1-arevalo-diana.bio: Former Texas State Representative for House District 116 and Managing Director of Advocacy for the ALS Association.

positions.stance: Wants taxpayers to have clear information about BCAD decisions, spending and the appraisal process, with accessible public meetings.
Supports clearer communication, improved assistance, multilingual resources and better education about exemptions and the protest process.
Supports an appraisal system that treats every property owner fairly, "regardless of their neighborhood or ZIP code."
Supports qualified, impartial Appraisal Review Board members and consistent hearing standards in the protest process.

tx-bexar-2026-bcad-p2-hizel-erika.name: Erika Hizel
tx-bexar-2026-bcad-p2-hizel-erika.bio: Founding President of the San Antonio Property Owners Alliance and a housing provider and small business owner.

positions.stance: Wants clear communication of how properties are appraised, valued and taxed.
Supports public meetings and forums so taxpayers can give input on valuation processes and tax calculations.
Supports regular updates about changes in tax policies, rates, appraisal processes and valuation assessments.
